title: Readings in Distributed Systems
abstract: This post is a collection of readings on distributed systems, compiled by Christopher Meiklejohn. It includes references to notable distributed systems papers and books that have influenced the field.
summary:
The document titled "Readings in Distributed Systems" is not a traditional academic paper with primary research results but rather a curated list of seminal papers and resources in the field of distributed systems, compiled by Christopher Meiklejohn. It serves as a reference for those seeking foundational and influential works in distributed systems research. 

Christopher Meiklejohn has highlighted seminal works addressing various aspects of distributed systems such as consistency models, replication, fault-tolerance, and concurrency, which are pivotal to understanding the complexities involved in designing distributed systems.

While the entry itself is a resource compilation, many of the cited works within this compilation have significantly influenced the distributed systems domain. For instance, papers addressing the CAP theorem and eventual consistency have guided research and practical applications in designing scalable and robust distributed systems. Meiklejohn's compilation could influence readers by directing them towards these key readings, subsequently impacting their understanding and further research pursuits.

No direct citations of this specific post were found in the academic literature during a search; however, the referenced works within the compilation are frequently cited in distributed systems research.
